channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Thanksgiving storm damages buildings, floods streets, causes power outages
item.description: Gov. Kathy Hochul's office declared a State of Emergency on Thanksgiving.

item.title: Spain's De Cos chosen as next ECB president
item.description: European leaders have agreed to nominate the former head of the Bank of Spain as the next president of the European Central Bank. Pablo ​Hernandez ‌de ⁠Cos will replace the outgoing Christine Lagarde as the bank faces pressure to tackle high inflation, borrowing costs, and government debt. Also in the show - US regulators give SpaceX the green light to send satellites for data centers into space, and American households face higher costs for their Thanksgiving celebrations.

item.title: Nigeria faces rising election violence in run up to vote
item.description: In tonight's edition, concerns are mounting that electoral violence could deter voters from taking part in Nigeria’s presidential election in January. Also, the driver of a car suspected of causing a fuel tanker to overturn on a major highway in Egypt is detained. And Sierra Leone was once considered the most dangerous place in the world to give birth. Today, maternal deaths have dropped dramatically.

item.title: Iranian monarchists disrupt Paris event, highlighting bitter diaspora divide
item.description: A Paris event on Iranian women's rights attended by French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot was disrupted when diaspora supporters of Reza Pahlavi, the US-based son of Iran's deposed shah, taunted left-leaning opponents of Iran's Islamic regime. The chaos underscored the bitter divides in the Iranian diaspora as the Iran war enters its tenth month.

item.title: Sanchez's big gamble: Will Spain swing from Socialists to hard right?
item.description: For eight years, he’s been a mainstay among European leaders, one who’s snatched victory from the jaws of defeat before but has Pedro Sanchez run out of road this time? Spain's Socialist prime minister dogged by incumbent fatigue and nepotism allegations. Sanchez gambled on turning the rift in his coalition over his country's housing shortage into a referendum on his country's strong growth and calling a snap general election.

item.title: Hamas weighs response after Israel kills 10 people in Gaza
item.description: Five Israeli strikes and a shooting overnight and on Thursday killed 10 Palestinians across Gaza, according to officials at Shifa and Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospitals, where the casualties were taken. A strike on a residential apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza killed a man and his wife, the officials said. FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin speaks with journalist Ahmed Dremly, who was in Gaza until six months ago and has extensively covered the humanitarian crisis there.

item.title: Trump urges Putin to end 'military aggression' in Europe
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a shift in tone towards the leader Russian he called his friend just a week ago. Trump said he had made the request to Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. The US leader's comments come a day after he hosted NATO chief Mark Rutte in Florida, after which they issued a joint statement calling on Russia not to expand the Ukraine war. FRANCE 24's international affairs editor Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

item.title: France's Bardella faces new allegations of anti-Semitic comments
item.description: French far-right leader Jordan Bardella on Thursday faced new accusations of having made anti-Semitic remarks as a teenager, after French media published extracts from previously unaired conversations online. The 31-year-old top ally of French presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has denied any wrongdoing after allegations emerged in September that he made conspiracist comments about Jewish people on Facebook in 2013. FRANCE 24's Solange Mougin reports.

item.title: Le Pen slams push for EU budget deal before French election
item.description: EU leaders locked horns over the bloc's budget at a summit meeting in Brussels on Thursday, as far-right leader Marine Le Pen slammed an "underhanded" push to lock in the long-term spending plans before French presidential elections next year. European Council head Antonio Costa turned up the pressure upon arrival at the budget talks, where heavyweight Germany is pressing for cuts as well as burden-sharing on money for Ukraine. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

item.title: Mexican president blasts DEA over tip lines
item.description: Mexico's president has criticized the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration for setting up anonymous tip lines in the country

item.title: Marie-Antoinette’s porcelain ‘nipple bowl’ fetches record $3.1 million at Paris auction
item.description: A "jatte-teton", or nipple bowl, that once belonged to French Queen Marie-Antoinette fetched a record €2.9 million ($3.1 million) at Paris auction Thursday. The breast-shaped porcelain bowl was one of four such pieces which King Louis XVI once ordered for his queen's royal dairy creamery.

item.title: Bands drum up support so the show goes on for postponed Macy's Thanksgiving parade
item.description: Bands from across the country are drumming up support to stay in New York City through the weekend for the now-postponed 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

item.title: French far-right leader Jordan Bardella faces fresh allegations of anti-Semitism
item.description: The leader of France's far-right National Rally party, Jordan #Bardella, is facing fresh accusations of having made anti-Semitic remarks as a teenager. On Thursday, November 26, French media outlets Mediapart and Le Monde published new excerpts from private Facebook conversations dating back to 2013.

item.title: WATCH: The tradition of Thanksgiving
item.description: ABC News' Michelle Franzen takes us to Plymouth, Massachusetts, where the tradition of Thanksgiving began when English settlers shared a meal with native tribes.

item.title: Reporters Without Borders demands suspension of controversial French TV channel CNews
item.description: Paris-based international press freedom group Reporters Without Borders (RSF) on Thursday called on France's media regulator Arcom to suspend right-wing channel CNews for one month over its failure to uphold pluralism. The news channel owned by conservative billionaire Vincent Bolloré condemned the call for its suspension.

item.title: Driver suspected of causing tanker crash in Egypt that killed 31 detained
item.description: The driver of a car suspected to have caused a fuel tanker to overturn in Egypt, causing the deaths of 31 people, has been detained.

item.title: Witnesses contacted as US probe into World Cup sell-off plan intensifies
item.description: A planned US congressional investigation into FIFA and Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell-off plans is intensifying with requests to speak to current and former FIFA staff, Sky News understands.

item.title: Iran live updates: Iranian drone attack killed 2 Italians, Kuwait says
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Will Spain's far right replace Europe's left-wing stalwart?
item.description: Some 39 million Spaniards will head to the ballot this Sunday to vote in early general elections. Latest polls put the conservative Popular Party ahead of incumbent PM Pedro Sanchez’s Socialists. The third-strongest political force, however, is the far-right Vox party. A strong showing at Sunday’s election could see them form Spain’s next government. FRANCE 24 explains.

item.title: Airline suspends all flights - as carrier faces bankruptcy
item.description: Norse Atlantic Airways has suspended all flights, with the company saying it could file for bankruptcy unless an urgent solution to its finances is found.

item.title: ACROSS AFRICA: Tunisian Photographer's Family Focus
item.description: Stories from the continent with Georja Calvin-Smith. This week, health workers struggling to keep pace with DR Congo's Ebola outbreak say they feel abandoned and unsupported. Also, the World Cup was about more than winning... for some fans, at least. Tunisia's performance may not have been all that its supporters had hoped, but sports photographer Hosni Manoubi is far from negative about a family tradition of documenting his country's international sports showings. [Archive Episode, June 2026]

item.title: In California, exceptional tides and nearly 9m-high waves batter the coast
item.description: USA: Powerful waves and king tides destroyed part of a pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, on Wednesday. In Marin County, authorities issued a temporary evacuation order and urged people to stay away from the beach.

item.title: Spanish economist de Cos to succeed Lagarde as head of ECB
item.description: Spanish monetary economist Pablo Hernandez de Cos on Thursday was set to replace France's Christine Lagarde as the new head of the European Central Bank (ECB). His nomination comes as the Europe's most powerful financial institution grapples with an Iran war-driven resurgence in inflation and a cost of living crisis.

item.title: Lost homes, stolen freedom: National Book Award winners on exile and imprisonment
item.description: Two books about losing everything have just won America's most prestigious literary honours. Hannah Lillith Assadi took the National Book Award for fiction for "Paradiso 17", a novel inspired by her late father, who was driven from Palestine in 1948 during the Nakba. Abdelrahman ElGendy won the non-fiction prize for "Huna", his memoir of six years as a political prisoner in Egypt, arrested at 17 alongside his father. ElGendy couldn't be in New York to collect his award: his visa was denied.

item.title: How far-right Vox is winning over young voters ahead of Spain's snap election
item.description: Spain's Vox party is winning over many young people ahead of the country's snap election on November 29, particularly men. The far-right party is capitalising on the rising cost of living and anti-immigrant sentiment to expand its once-marginal electoral base.

item.title: Across Africa: The Scars of South Africa's Soweto Uprising
item.description: 50 years ago, thousands of young South Africans from Soweto protested against apartheid's stranglehold on their education and the imposition of Afrikaans as a language of instruction. What began as a peaceful protest ended in bloodshed. And men in Northern Benin confront uncomfortable realities about the lives of the women who live and love them. [Archive edition, June 2026]

item.title: From leadership crises to tech outages, can corporations rebuild public trust?
item.description: From cyberattacks to network failures to leadership crises, tech corporations are showing signs of vulnerability. The dramatic resignation and return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has underscored the potential risk of depending on a single leader, both for the company and the entire AI industry. Meanwhile, global outages at Microsoft and a number of US banks have showcased declining public trust in institutions.

item.title: French woman on trial for IS group propaganda tells court she’s ‘ashamed’
item.description: The trial of Émilie König, one of France's most high-profile Islamic State (IS) group recruits, opened in a Paris court on Thursday with the 41-year-old mother of five apologising to her children, mother and the "French nation" for her actions. König travelled in 2012 to Syria, where she appeared in the jihadist group's propaganda videos. She was repatriated to France in 2022.

item.title: Season's eatings! Celebrating Thanksgiving in France
item.description: This Thursday marks Thanksgiving in the United States, the biggest travel holiday of the year there and arguably the most important on US calendars. But here in France, it's just another day. However, Americans living in Paris do try to capture the Thanksgiving spirit, though it can be tricky to track down the turkeys and pies required. Joining us to discuss how Americans do Thanksgiving in Paris is Cordon Bleu-trained chef and the owner of Boneshaker Donuts, Amanda Bankert.

item.title: Madagascar's near-total abortion ban puts women's lives at risk
item.description: November 25 marked the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Activists argue that tackling gender-based violence also means addressing the wider inequalities that put women at risk, including restrictions on reproductive rights. In Madagascar, abortion is almost entirely banned, even in cases of rape, incest or when a woman's life is at risk. FRANCE 24’s Aurélie Kouman reports on the consequences of the country's strict laws, which force thousands of women to seek unsafe, clandestine procedures.

item.title: Fighting in eastern Congo forces Ebola workers to evacuate, disrupts outbreak response
item.description: Escalating fighting in eastern Congo has forced Ebola response workers to leave affected areas and disrupted efforts to contain the deadliest outbreak in the country, health officials and humanitarian workers said Wednesday. Congo’s Ebola outbreak has infected more than 11,700 people and killed more than 5,700 since it was declared in May, according to the latest government data. FRANCE 24's Emmet Livingstone reports from Kinshasa, DR Congo.

item.title: Moscow drone incursions: Poland to create no-fly zone at Ukraine border
item.description: Poland will soon create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, a deputy defence minister announced on Wednesday, after several incursions into its airspace it blamed on Russia. Poland backs Ukraine as it fights off Russia's near five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Moscow of seeking to target Kyiv's supporters with drone incursions and other methods.

item.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
item.description: As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease.

item.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
item.description: Leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the U.S. and South Korea.

item.title: Security incident reported at Royal Navy headquarters
item.description: Police responded to what appears to have been a hoax bomb threat at a Royal Navy training site.

item.title: WATCH: NYPD releases new images in manhole mystery
item.description: In the latest on the ongoing manhole mystery in New York City, the NYPD has released new images of suspects seen exiting a manhole last week.

item.title: Charity set up in honour of Princess Diana placed into administration
item.description: A charity set up in tribute to the late Princess Diana has been placed into administration.

item.title: WATCH: Women around the world fight for gender equity in sumo
item.description: For more than 1,500 years, professional sumo has only allowed men into the ring. Nightline traveled to Japan to learn more about the ancient ban and meet with athletes fighting against tradition.

item.title: WATCH: Man uses balloon art to pay off $400K in student loans
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a doctor in New York who's using his balloon twisting talents to help him pay off his student loan debt.

item.title: Myanmar says it will not comply with 'inappropriate' ICJ genocide orders
item.description: Myanmar's leader has said his government will not ‌comply with all measures ordered by a top international court after it was found guilty of committing genocide against the Rohingya minority.

item.title: At Albuquerque's Indian Pueblo Kitchen, Native American dishes are the main course
item.description: At an Albuquerque, N.M., museum, the restaurant is just as much of a draw as the exhibitions, with dishes like green chile stew and sweet biscochitos flavored with anise and cinnamon.

item.title: 'Memories of a Good Meal': How food made a difference during WWII
item.description: New Orleans Chef Alon Shaya's new cookbook shares stories of resilience from World War II, centered around food.

item.title: Dubai wholesaler plans renewed bid for collapsed Poundland
item.description: The Dubai-based businessman who emerged as a suitor for Poundland days before its collapse into insolvency is planning a fresh bid to buy the retailer out of administration.

item.title: A dish with a story, Thanksgiving with culinary historian Michael Twitty
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel welcomes culinary historian Michael Twitty into her kitchen for a Thanksgiving cooking session on making Kush, the forerunner to Southern cornbread dressing.

item.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
item.description: The Trump administration gave Elon Musk's SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a move that has raised skepticism among scientists.

item.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
item.description: Taylor revealed his battle with Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer in 2022. He was the guitarist of the 1980s English band Duran Duran, whose pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf" and "Rio".

item.title: Major US tech index comes close to crashing into a bear market
item.description: A tech-heavy index on Wall Street briefly teetered into bear market territory on Wednesday - as AI-exposed stocks continue to face heavy sell-offs.

item.title: WATCH: Tips for staying healthy and keeping the peace at the Thanksgiving table
item.description: Nutrition specialist J.J. Virgin and etiquette expert Thomas Farley discuss how you can navigate some of Thanksgiving's tricky problems.

item.title: Trump admin proposes new tariffs on China, EU and 12 other trading partners
item.description: A senior admin official said the countries were informed of proposed tariffs.

item.title: US authorises SpaceX to deploy one million satellites to space
item.description: The US' Federal Communications Commission is authorising SpaceX to send a million satellites for data centres in space, the agency said.

item.title: WATCH: DoorDash aims to deliver 2M meals to food banks for free
item.description: Daniel Riff, head of global food access programs for DoorDash, discusses the company's initiative.

item.title: WATCH: 'Dancing with the Stars' superfan gets special surprise
item.description: A lucky superfan receives two tickets to the "Dancing with the Stars" live show on Feb. 16, including a behind-the-scenes tour, a meet-and-greet and exclusive merchandise.

item.title: WATCH: Best and worst times to drive
item.description: ABC News' Rhiannon Ally provides the latest updates on the road as gas prices drop, offering some relief for drivers this Thanksgiving.

item.title: WATCH: Thanksgiving travel rush underway
item.description: Major airlines already offering travel waivers in the wake of the Thanksgiving travel rush as a collision between a plane and catering truck at JFK airport creates delays.

item.title: 'The threat is finally real': Judge rips White House 'weaponization'
item.description: A D.C. magistrate judge has issued a scathing written order ripping the Trump administration for what he described as the blatant "weaponization" of law enforcement.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Melania Trump reunites seventh group of Ukrainian and Russian children with families
item.description: The White House says Melania Trump has helped return a seventh group of Ukrainian and Russian children to their families

item.title: Treasury's financial crimes agency says it's investigating 'cybersecurity incident'
item.description: The agency handles sensitive information and reports about financial crimes.

item.title: WATCH: Australian man bikes 10,000 miles across 48 US states
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to ultra cyclist Jack Thompson, who rode through all 48 states in the contiguous U.S., covering almost 10,000 miles in 60 days.

item.title: WATCH: This American Wonder: David Muir journeys inside Statue of Liberty 140 years later
item.description: David Muir climbs to the top of the Statue of Liberty – sharing her history and meaning on its 140th birthday.

item.title: Two children among six dead in plane crash
item.description: Divers have found the bodies of six people, including two children, after a plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi on Tuesday, according to the US Coast Guard.

item.title: Trump awards Medal of Freedom to former NYC Mayor Rudy Giuliani
item.description: Trump pardoned Giuliani last year.

item.title: Colombian police storm supermarket, freeing hostages and killing gunman
item.description: Colombian police have stormed a supermarket and freed at least 20 people who were being held hostage, killing one of the gunmen.

item.title: They want to watch Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan die but the Army won’t let them
item.description: Julia Wilson was nine months pregnant when she found herself caught in gunfire at Fort Hood in 2009. 'It's crazy how quickly things run through your brain," she said.

item.title: Groups push back on Trump administration changes to historical monument
item.description: Two Philadelphia groups filed a federal lawsuit against the Trump administration over the removal of panels at the slavery memorial at the President’s House site.

item.title: WATCH: Detroit Lions help feed their community this Thanksgiving
item.description: ABC News' Will Reeve shares how the Detroit Lions are carrying on a Thanksgiving tradition of giving back to those in need.

item.title: Trump owned at least $12 million in Nvidia stock at the end of last year
item.description: President Donald Trump owned at least $12 million in Nvidia stock at the end of 2025, according to his annual financial disclosure report reviewed by ABC News.
